words.said: Research: Zenod as a company memory, one voice-note mailbox every employee sends ideas to, AI sorts them and bubbles things up; one page on who would buy it, what exists, how it differs from EpicTeam
words.where: the row's ask (no quote of his found)
words.how: Evidence page shows the IN, ZENOD DOES, OUT company memory diagram, buyers, a what-exists table, and a How it differs section against EpicTeam.

visual.summary: At 390 px the punchline box opens the page, then the three product flows stack as boxes with arrows; at 1280 px they sit side by side. No sideways scroll, text fits, and the evidence page needs no feedback block.

held: ambiguous: "The team recommends yes, after the tester invite." Reading one: the team waits for the tester invite to be sent before it starts, so your yes is only the first step. Reading two: the invite is a step you already have to approve, so your yes starts the test now. Your answer and what you do next depend on which one is meant.
